newsitem.title: USA: US FCC rejects request to set aside phone rules.
newsitem.headline: US FCC rejects request to set aside phone rules.

text.p: The Federal Communications Commission Tuesday rejected requests by three local telephone companies to set aside new rules designed to break open the local phone market to competition.
GTE Corp, Southern New England Telephone Co (SNET) and U S West Inc had asked the agency to stay its August 8 "interconnection" rules. GTE and SNET had filed their requests jointly.
The FCC, in its ruling, said the requests for a stay were unjustified under the test used to evaluate such motions.
It said the phone companies failed to demonstrate they would suffer "irreperable harm" if a stay was not granted or that the public interest favored a stay.

The regulations require, among other things, the Baby Bell companies and other local carriers to lease space on their phone lines to new rivals -- such as long-distance companies and cable-TV operators -- at discounts of 17 percent to 25 percent.
The Baby Bells and state regulators also are seeking to overturn the FCC rules in federal court. Lawyers, however, believe the companies and regulators are unlikely to succeed.
